sentences.text: THE STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH AND OTHERS

Appearance:
 Shri Abhijeet Tripathi - Advocate for the petitioner.
Shri Y. Shukla - PL for the respondents/ State.

ORDER This petition is filed seeking the following reliefs :-
7.1.

Issue a writ in the nature of mandamus directing the respondents to follow the due procedure contemplated in Land Acquisition Act for acquisition of the lands of the petitioner in question in accordance with law.

7.2. To direct the respondents to compensate the petitioner suitably for his valuable land/house in question with all the benefits extended by formulating the Rehabilitation policy in lieu of acquisition being made for the project of the respondent concerned, by considering and deciding his representation made to redress his grievance.

7.3 Pass any other writ/order/direction to which this Hon'ble Court deems fit and proper under the circumstances of the case including the cost of the petition."
2.

Briefly stated facts of the case are that the petitioner is a Patta holder of the land bearing khasra No. 153/2/N, and 173/4/N situated at village Amlori Halka Nogar, Waidhan District Singrouli and having his name recorded in the revenue record, has been in title and possession of the said land Dasharam Vaishya vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161837721/
1 since the year 1981-82.

sentences.text:
The petitioner has also annexed the relevant NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-JBP:17945 2 WP-21179-2013 documents vide Annexures P/1 to P/3.

Since the outer limit of two yeas to have effected and completed all the proceeding of making an acquisition of the lands also envisaged in section 6 of the Act was fixed with a condition if it is failed to do so within such a stipulated period then all the acquisition proceedings if made, would stand lapsed and owner of the land or person interested in the land is made free to deal with the land as unencumbered land and

seeking the proceeding again required as per law after having received the NOC and de-notifying the lands in question, and to proceed in accordance with law and provisions contained in Land Acquisition Act, the inhabitants of village Amlori submitted objection/application U/s 9(2)
of the Act vide Annexure P-5.

The petitioner agitating the act of respondent have also made his representation and sought to be compensated him suitably as per market price, but nothing was done and considered to the redressal of his grievance mere keeping it pending as turned down by respondent so far.

3. On notice being issued, the respondents/State have filed return and brought to the notice of this Court an order dated 30.9.2011 passed by the respondents, whereby claim of the petitioner regarding compensation has been rejected on the ground that the petitioner has occupied the government land and fraudulently has got recorded his name in the revenue records.
The said order is not put to challenge in the present petition.
There are specific finding recorded by the respondents while passing the impugned order declaring the petitioner not entitled for compensation.
4. As the order passed by the respondents is not put to challenge, no relief can be extended to the petitioner.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:17945 3 WP-21179-2013 5.
However, liberty is extended to the petitioner to challenge the order passed by the authorities in an appropriate proceedings.
6. With the aforesaid, the petition stands disposed of.

(VISHAL MISHRA) JUDGE JP Dasharam Vaishya vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161837721/
